goal: Make verify.Next artifact-driven for every triage state (stale, yes, dry_run, failed, no) so runs verify returns a directly actionable command on success paths.
background:
Acceptance criteria:
- When triage state is stale, verify.Next returns 'bakeoff triage <run-id> --force' (carrying --out when provided).
- When triage state is current (final.json + triage.md present, hashes match), verify.Next returns 'bakeoff show <run-id> --triage'.
- When triage/status.json reports status='dry_run' and no current triage exists, verify.Next returns 'bakeoff triage <run-id> --force'.
- When triage was attempted but failed (triage/status.json status is present and not 'ok' or 'dry_run', final.json/triage.md absent), verify.Next returns 'bakeoff triage <run-id> --force'.
- When no triage artifacts exist (status.json absent, final.json absent), verify.Next continues to return 'bakeoff show <run-id>' (no --triage flag).
- When exitCode != 0, behavior is unchanged: returns bakeoff rerun command when work-order.json exists, else the existing restore-artifacts message.
- verify.Result.Triage.State exposes the same artifact-driven state set Next routes on; 'failed' joins the existing 'yes'/'stale'/'dry_run'/'no' values when status.json shows a failed attempt.
- Decisions are artifact-driven: only triage/final.json, triage/triage.md, triage/status.json, decision.json, work-order.json, and provider failure files are consulted; report.md prose is not parsed for routing.
- Focused unit tests in internal/verify/verify_test.go cover stale, yes, dry_run, failed, no, and error-path branches and pass under 'go test ./internal/verify ./internal/triage'.

Edit boundary:
- internal/verify/verify.go
- internal/verify/verify_test.go
- internal/triage/state.go (only if a small artifact-driven helper is needed)
Bakeoff will capture candidate patches from isolated worktrees and will not apply them to this checkout.

build.comparison_goal: Prefer the patch that satisfies the acceptance criteria with the smallest maintainable change.
